Deadline check

Tell us what arrived and when. We count the days the way the court will.

Pick the day to see your deadline. Three weeks from the day the letter reached you, to file a claim with the labour court (§ 4 KSchG). A weekend or a public holiday moves the last day to the next working day.

A guide, not advice. A letter counts as received on the day it landed in your letterbox, opened or not.

Practice

Two fields, one side of the table

Because we never act for employers or landlords, we never meet a former client across the table. Every topic below comes with the deadline that decides it.

Employment law for employees

Dismissal and unfair-dismissal claims

Most dismissals after six months in a company with more than ten staff need a reason. Whether yours has one is decided by the labour court - if you ask it in time.3 weeks from receipt (§ 4 KSchG)

Settlement and severance agreements

There is rarely a legal right to severance - it is negotiated. We read the offer, the numbers and the wording with you.signing can stop unemployment benefit for 12 weeks (§ 159 SGB III)

Fixed-term contracts

A fixed term without a reason is allowed for two years at most, renewed no more than three times. After that, the contract may already be permanent.3 weeks after the agreed end (§ 17 TzBfG)

References, unpaid wages and overtime

Coded phrases in a reference, a bonus that never came, hours nobody paid for.many contracts cut claims off after 3 months

Tenancy law for tenants

Rent increases and the rent brake

We check the increase against Cologne's rent index and the cap of 15 % in three years that applies in the city.to the end of the 2nd month after receipt (§ 558b BGB)

Service-charge statements

Heating, caretaker, insurance - what may be passed on, and what a statement that arrives too late can no longer ask for.12 months to object after receipt (§ 556 BGB)

Notice for the landlord's own use

Is the need real, is the notice long enough, and does your situation outweigh it? Age, illness and school years count.objection 2 months before the tenancy ends (§ 574b BGB)

Defects, rent reduction and the deposit

Mould, a broken heating system, a deposit that does not come back.a deposit may not exceed three months' net rent (§ 551 BGB)

How a mandate works

From the first call to the hearing

  1. 01

    You call or write

    Tell us what you received and when. We call back within one working day - the same day when a deadline is close.

  2. 02

    The first consultation

    45 minutes at the office, by phone or by video, for a fixed €190 plus VAT. You leave knowing your deadline, your chances and the cost of each next step.

  3. 03

    The mandate

    If you instruct us, you sign a power of attorney and, where we charge by the hour, a written fee agreement. We ask your legal expenses insurer for cover.

  4. 04

    Letter, claim, settlement

    We write to the other side or file the claim. In a dismissal case the labour court holds a first hearing within weeks, and most cases settle there.

Questions

What people ask in the first call

My employer dismissed me by email. Is that valid?

No. A dismissal must be a signed letter on paper (§ 623 BGB) - email, text message and WhatsApp are void. Call us anyway: the employer often sends the letter a few days later, and that starts the three weeks.

Do I have a right to severance pay?

Usually not by law. Severance is what an employer pays to end a claim it might lose. A common starting point is half a month's gross salary per year of service - what you get depends on how strong your claim is.

Should I sign the settlement agreement I was handed?

Not on the spot. Signing it can cost you twelve weeks of unemployment benefit, and it ends any claim. Ask for a few days - an employer who refuses is telling you something.

My landlord wants more rent. Do I have to agree?

Only to an increase that is justified - up to the local comparative rent, at most 15 % in three years in Cologne. You have until the end of the second month after the letter arrived. Do not simply pay the new amount: that can count as consent.

What should I bring to the first consultation?

The letter and its envelope, your contract, your last three payslips - or your tenancy agreement and the last two service-charge statements. And a note of the day the letter arrived.

Do you take cases outside Cologne?

Yes. We appear before every labour court in Germany, and most of the work runs by phone and video. A tenancy case is heard by the local court where the flat is.

Professional title and chamber

All lawyers hold the title Rechtsanwalt / Rechtsanwältin, conferred in the Federal Republic of Germany, and are members of the Rechtsanwaltskammer Köln, Riehler Straße 30, 50668 Köln, which supervises them. The specialist titles (Fachanwalt) were conferred by the same chamber.

Professional rules

The Federal Lawyers' Act (BRAO), the Professional Code for Lawyers (BORA), the Specialist Lawyers' Code (FAO), the Lawyers' Remuneration Act (RVG), the Code of Conduct for European Lawyers (CCBE) and the Act on European Lawyers in Germany (EuRAG). The Federal Bar publishes them at brak.de.

Professional liability insurance

Domstadt Versicherung AG, Kaiser-Wilhelm-Ring 9, 50672 Köln. Cover: the European Union, at least €2.5 million per claim, as the law requires of a PartG mbB.

Disputes with consumers

A dispute about our fees can go to the conciliation board of the legal profession, Schlichtungsstelle der Rechtsanwaltschaft, Neue Grünstraße 17, 10179 Berlin.

The consultation request

We use your name, phone number, email and description to call you back (Art. 6 (1) (b) GDPR) and to check that we have no conflict of interest, which the law requires of us before any advice (Art. 6 (1) (c) GDPR, § 43a (4) BRAO). Only the lawyers and the office manager see it.

How long we keep it

A request that does not lead to a mandate is deleted after six months. Mandate files are kept for six years after the mandate ends (§ 50 BRAO).

Professional secrecy

Everything you tell us is confidential under § 43a (2) BRAO and § 203 of the Criminal Code - also when you do not instruct us.

No cookies, no tracking

This site sets no cookies and counts no visitors. The look and the dark mode you pick are not stored.

Your rights

You may ask what we hold about you and have it corrected, restricted or deleted where the retention rules allow, and you may complain to the State Commissioner for Data Protection of North Rhine-Westphalia (LDI NRW).
